title: Enterprise Onboarding: Comprehensive Support, Integration, Escalation & QBR Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Purpose and scope

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended processes and templates for enterprise onboarding, technical integration, support escalation, known issues & workarounds, and QBR/health-check rhythms. It is intended for CSMs, Solutions Engineers, Support Engineers, and the customer's technical stakeholders. Use this document for: initial onboarding, handoffs from sales, recurring health checks, and incident escalation during the first 90-180 days of production usage.

Key goals
- Reliable handoff from Sales to Customer Success and Engineering.
- Fast, low-friction technical integration with clear ownership.
- Predictable escalation paths with SLA targets and contact methods.
- Standardized QBR and health-check artifacts to measure success and catch regressions early.

Audience
- Customer Success Managers (CSM)
- Solutions Engineers (SE) / Integration Engineers
- Support Engineers (L1/L2)
- Engineering owners (runtime, infra, product)
- Customer technical leads and platform engineers

1) Pre-kickoff checklist (owner: CSM)
- Confirm contract-level entitlements: Dedicated vs Hosted, regions, data residency, retention.
- Validate account: API keys, team org ID, billing contact, support tier, and LDAP/SAML needs.
- Gather integration artifacts from customer: sample prompts, expected throughput, sequence lengths, and sensitive data classifications.
- Schedule 60-90 minute kickoff meeting with agenda, invitees, and preliminary SLOs.

2) Kickoff agenda (owner: CSM / SE)
1. Introductions and roles/contacts.
2. High-level architecture and security review (VPC, KMS, network allow-lists).
3. Integration plan and timeline (staging -> canary -> prod).
4. Success metrics and QBR cadence.
5. Escalation contacts and response SLAs.
6. Action items and owners.

3) Integration guide (owner: SE)
- Recommended environments: dev (integration), staging (pre-prod), prod.
- API keys: create scoped test keys, rotate after canary.
- Rate limits & quotas: provide per-customer baseline and burst plan.
- Test prompts & eval harness: seed the customer's prompt set into the eval harness and run baseline quality checks.
- Observability hooks: ensure application-level tracing correlated with Redwood request_id.
- Security checklist: IP allow-list, VPC peering setup (if Private), KMS/HSM integration for Private deployments.

Example quick integration commands
- Create test key (Hosted): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>" -d '{"name":"acme-test-key"}'
- Basic generation test: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <test-key>" -d '{"model":"redwood/open-7b", "input":"Hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

4) Onboarding checklist (owner: SE + CSM)
- Day 0-7: account provisioning, test keys, first successful generation/embedding call.
- Day 7-21: traffic shaping in staging, validate latency and error rates at target throughput.
- Day 21-45: canary deployment with subset of traffic in prod, monitor metrics and regressions.
- Day 45-90: full roll-out and QBR 1 (initial health review and optimization plan).

Deliverables and ownership table
| Deliverable | Owner | Target date | Acceptance criteria |
|-------------|-------|-------------|---------------------|
| Account provisioning | CSM | Day 0 | API keys, billing, contacts confirmed |
| Integration test runbook | SE | Day 7 | Successful calls, trace correlation |
| Canary plan | SE + Eng | Day 21 | Canary run, rollback plan documented |
| QBR deck (initial) | CSM + SE | Day 45 | Metrics baseline and action items |

5) Support process & SLAs (owner: Support Manager)
- Triage flow: L1 receives ticket -> reproduce -> route to L2/SE if code/config issue -> escalate to Eng SRE/runtime for P1.
- Response SLA (business hours unless customer has 24x7):
  - P1 (service down / customer-facing outage): initial response within 15 minutes, dedicated incident channel, follow-up every 30 minutes.
  - P2 (degraded experience / increased error rate): initial response within 1 hour, updates every 2 hours.
  - P3 (non-critical bug / integration question): initial response within 4 business hours.
- Escalation channels: primary Slack channel #cs-support, PagerDuty for oncall, dedicated customer escalation email.

Escalation matrix (simplified)
- L1 Support -> L2 Support (SE) -> Eng SRE/runtime -> Product/Engineering (if bug/regression) -> Exec on-call for SLA breaches.

6) Escalation playbook (owner: Support Lead)
Severity definitions and steps:
- P1 (Critical outage)
  1. Open incident in incident management tool and assign P1.
  2. Notify on-call via PagerDuty and create Slack incident channel #incident-<customer>-<id>.
  3. Triage: collect logs, request_id(s), timestamp range, and recent deploys.
  4. If a code regression suspected, trigger rollback or fallback to a compatible model variant.
  5. Customer comms: CSM sends initial incident notification within 30 minutes and hourly updates.
  6. Post-incident: follow standard postmortem within 72 hours.
- P2 (Degraded performance / quality)
  1. Collect traces and performance metrics (p95/p99 latency, error rate).
  2. Ramp control: reduce throughput or route to dedicated capacity if available.
  3. Execute mitigation playbooks (model fallback, quantization profile change, increase memory headroom).
  4. CSM provides status update within 2 hours.
- P3 (Support question / non-urgent bug)
  1. Acknowledge ticket and assign to SE/Support.
  2. Provide workaround or timeline for permanent fix.

Contact list (example placeholders - owner: Support Ops)
- 24x7 PagerDuty: eng-sre-oncall@redwood.ai (use PagerDuty).
- Primary Slack channels: #cs-support, #runtime-oncall.
- Escalation email (exec): escalation@redwood.ai.

7) Known issues & common workarounds (owner: SE + Eng)
- ISSUE ID: KI-2026-001 – Increased latency after model variant switch
  - Symptom: sudden p99 latency increase following automated fallback to a newer model variant.
  - Root cause (typical): kernel mismatch or quantization profile misconfiguration on Dedicated pool.
  - Workaround: pin model to previous verified variant, clear local KV cache for affected sessions, and restart workers in a rolling fashion.
  - Permanent fix: coordinate with serving-runtime to add variant smoke-tests and gating before fallback.
- ISSUE ID: KI-2026-002 – Tokenization mismatch on embeddings
  - Symptom: embedding similarity scores shift after tokenizer library bump.
  - Workaround: re-run embeddings for active index segments, or freeze tokenizer version in deployment.
  - Notes: add tokenizer version to model metadata and include in QBR metrics.
- ISSUE ID: KI-2026-003 – Synthetic requests cause quota exhaustion in staging
  - Symptom: burst of automated QA traffic consumes quota and affects canary.
  - Workaround: enable rate-limiting tags for test keys and isolate synthetic traffic into a separate quota bucket.

Include a triage checklist for new issues:
1. Reproduce with customer's request_id (if available).
2. Correlate with infra events / deploys.
3. Identify whether issue is config, integration, model, or infra.
4. Apply short-term mitigation and document as a known issue if repeatable.

8) Health checks and QBR materials (owner: CSM)
- Recommended cadence: first QBR at 45-60 days after production, then quarterly until stable, then biannually for low-touch accounts.
- Core metrics to present in QBR:
  - Availability / uptime (target: 99.9% for Hosted; contract-defined for Dedicated).
  - Latency: p50/p95/p99 for generation and embedding calls.
  - Error rate: 4xx/5xx split and top error codes.
  - Cost metrics: cost per 1k tokens, cost per embedding, and unit economics vs baseline.
  - Quality metrics: eval pass rate on seed prompt set, regression alerts, and human-rated quality score if available.
  - Usage trends: top routes, peak QPS, and sequence length distribution.

QBR slide outline (template)
- Title slide: Customer, CSM, date, attendees
- Objectives and agenda
- Production health: availability, latency, error trends
- Quality: eval results, any regressions, action items
- Cost and optimization opportunities (batching, quantization, routing)
- Roadmap and feature requests
- Open actions and owner commitments

9) Postmortem & continuous improvement
- For every P1 incident, run a postmortem within 72 hours that includes timeline, impact, root cause, remediation, and action owner.
- Feed learnings into: model-serving-standards, infra runbooks, and the eval-harness.

10) Handoff to ongoing support (owner: CSM)
- When onboarding outcomes met (see acceptance criteria table), create a handoff ticket to Support with: production keys, canary logs, baseline metrics, and known issues list.
- Provide training session for Support and SRE on customer-specific integration.

Attachments and templates
- Onboarding kickoff checklist (copy & adapt)
- Incident channel naming convention: #incident-<customer>-<YYYYMMDD>-<id>
- Canary rollback checklist (technical and comms steps)
- QBR slide deck template (link placeholder)
